supporting_observations.claim: The reported window was around 13:40 UTC, but the records show an interactive logon at 13:40:11 and no PowerShell process launch until 13:44:46; the timing is close but not exact.
At 13:44:40, Maria's Word process opened Downloads\Statement.docm. About six seconds later, Word launched PowerShell with no profile, a hidden window, and an encoded command.

The encoded PowerShell command decodes to an expression that downloads and executes a script from raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1. Proxy records show a successful GET for that URL and a 200 status.
The PowerShell process launched rundll32.exe to call Init in C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll, and both processes subsequently exited.

The sequence of a macro-enabled document opening, hidden encoded PowerShell downloading and executing remote content, and rundll32 invoking a DLL in the user's roaming profile strongly supports malicious execution on the alerted workstation.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records show the downloaded script URL and successful HTTP status, but do not provide the script contents or prove what actions it performed (T023-00085, T023-00089).
The process command line identifies the DLL path and export invoked, but these records do not establish the DLL's contents or effects (T023-00096, T023-00097).
The provided records do not include PowerShell script-block or AMSI content, file hashes, or a DLL image-load record for svchelper.dll.
claims_not_established: The available records do not establish whether Maria intentionally opened Statement.docm or knew about the resulting execution (T023-00081, T023-00085).
The contents and behavior of the downloaded u.ps1 script and svchelper.dll are not established by the available records (T023-00089, T023-00096).
The records do not establish whether the activity persisted, accessed credentials, or exfiltrated data.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze Statement.docm, including its macro content and origin.
Retrieve the exact u.ps1 response and the svchelper.dll file; preserve hashes and determine their behavior.
Collect PowerShell operational/script-block and AMSI logs, endpoint detection telemetry, and relevant file-creation and persistence artifacts from WS-MLOPEZ-01.
Hunt across other hosts for the URL, script, DLL name or hash, and related process behavior.
unrelated_findings: At 14:03, a SYSTEM scheduled-task PowerShell process ran C:\Scripts\endpoint-inventory.ps1; at 14:05, that process generated an explicit-credentials event using svc-bkp for PROXY-HD-01. This is outside the alerted execution sequence and should be reviewed separately (T023-00165, T023-00166, T023-00168).
At 14:06, Edge accessed Slack. This is outside the alerted execution sequence and may warrant separate review against organizational policy (T023-00176, T023-00179, T023-00180).

At 14:16, Maria launched PowerShell to request https://packages.nuget.org/api/v2; this is outside the alerted execution sequence and should be assessed separately if relevant (T023-00265, T023-00266).
